about.lead: This is 2FAS Share. It lets you share passwords and notes through an encrypted link, with no account or installation. Closing this window does not use up the link.
about.step1: The sender enters the content, and it is encrypted in their browser.
about.step2: The decryption key stays in the link itself, after the # sign. The browser never sends this part of the link to the server.
about.step3: Only encrypted content reaches our server, and not even we can read it.
about.step4: You open the link, and the key decrypts the content on your device. The link disappears after the time the sender chose, or after the first open if they set it that way.
about.title: What is this page?
about.warningBody: Anyone with the full link can open the note, so check an unexpected link with the sender through another channel.
about.warningTitle: The link works like a key.

encryption.lead: The key used to encrypt it stays in the link itself, in the part after the # sign. That is the part browsers never send to the server.
encryption.leadNote: Without the full link, no one can read it, not even us.
encryption.note: Keep in mind that anyone who gets the full link can open the note, so send it only to people you trust.
encryption.step1Desc: You enter the content. It is encrypted right away in your browser.
encryption.step2Desc: The decryption key stays in the link itself, after the # sign.
encryption.step3Desc: It only gets encrypted data. It never sees the key.
encryption.step4Desc: The key from the link decrypts the content in their browser.
encryption.stepsNote: Content is encrypted in your browser, and the key stays in the link itself, never on our server.
encryption.title: Not even we can read your content

faq.a1:
Yes. Content is encrypted in the browser before it leaves your device. The key used to encrypt it stays in the link itself (after the # sign), and browsers never send that part to the server.

Without your link, not even we can read the content.
faq.a2: No. There is no sign-up and nothing to install. Enter the content, set the rules and create the link.
faq.a3: Yes. 2FAS Share is free to use, with no account and no limits. The code is open source, so anyone can check how it works.
faq.a4: Anyone who has the full link, and the password if you set one. With one-time access on, only the first person who opens it will see the content, so send the link only to people you trust.
faq.a5: The encrypted content is deleted from our server and the link stops working. Anyone who opens it later will only see that it no longer works.
faq.a6: An email or a message stays in inboxes, backups and chat histories for years. A 2FAS Share link disappears after the first open or after the time you choose, and the content is encrypted the whole way.
faq.a7: The link has already been opened or its time has run out, and the content cannot be recovered. Create a new link and send it again.
faq.q5: What happens after the link expires?
faq.q6: How is this different from email or a text message?
faq.q7: What if the recipient gets the error “This link no longer works”?
faq.title:
Short answers.
The rest is on GitHub.
